title: CTS The Gospel of John — Unit 10: The Way, the Truth, and the Life / The True Vine

blocks.en: 📖 The Gospel of John — Unit 10: The Way, the Truth, and the Life / The True Vine
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Evangelio de Juan — Unidad 10: El Camino, la Verdad y la Vida / La Vid Verdadera

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me." — John 14:6 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: ⚡ "Yo soy el camino, y la verdad, y la vida; nadie viene al Padre, sino por mí." — Juan 14:6 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — In the Upper Room
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — En el aposento alto

blocks.en: On the night before the cross, Jesus gathered His disciples in the upper room and gave them His final, most intimate teaching. It was, in a sense, their graduation from His seminary, with the Master Himself as the keynote speaker: summarizing what they must never forget, warning them of the trials to come, and pointing them to the truths they would live and die by. In these chapters two more of His great "I AM" sayings appear, and with them the seven are complete: the bread, the light, the door, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life — and now the way, and the true vine. The first tells us how to come to the Father; the second tells us how to stay alive once we have come. Together they answer the two deepest questions of the soul: How do I get home to God? And how do I live until I get there?
blocks.es_reference: La noche antes de la cruz, Jesús reunió a sus discípulos en el aposento alto y les dio su enseñanza final y más íntima. Fue, en cierto sentido, su graduación del seminario de él, con el Maestro mismo como orador principal: resumiendo lo que nunca deben olvidar, advirtiéndoles de las pruebas por venir, y señalándoles las verdades por las cuales vivirían y morirían. En estos capítulos aparecen dos más de sus grandes declaraciones "YO SOY", y con ellas las siete quedan completas: el pan, la luz, la puerta, el buen pastor, la resurrección y la vida — y ahora el camino, y la vid verdadera. La primera nos dice cómo venir al Padre; la segunda nos dice cómo permanecer vivos una vez que hemos venido. Juntas responden las dos preguntas más hondas del alma: ¿Cómo llego a casa, a Dios? Y ¿cómo vivo hasta llegar?

blocks.en: I. "Let Not Your Heart Be Troubled"
blocks.es_reference: I. "No se turbe vuestro corazón"

blocks.en: He begins with comfort, for their hearts were breaking: "Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in Me. In My Father's house are many mansions... I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to Myself; that where I am, there you may be also" (John 14:1–3). Heaven is not wishful thinking or "pie in the sky." It is a real place — the Father's house, the believer's true home. The word translated "mansions" simply means rooms, abiding places; we are not promised marble palaces but a place prepared by Christ Himself, and every prepared place will be beautiful.
blocks.es_reference: Comienza con consuelo, pues sus corazones se rompían: ⚡ "No se turbe vuestro corazón; creéis en Dios, creed también en mí. En la casa de mi Padre muchas moradas hay... voy, pues, a preparar lugar para vosotros. Y si me fuere y os preparare lugar, vendré otra vez, y os tomaré a mí mismo, para que donde yo estoy, vosotros también estéis" (Juan 14:1–3). El cielo no es una ilusión ni "pastel en el cielo." Es un lugar real — la casa del Padre, el verdadero hogar del creyente. La palabra traducida "moradas" significa simplemente habitaciones, lugares para morar; no se nos prometen palacios de mármol sino un lugar preparado por Cristo mismo, y cada lugar preparado será hermoso.

blocks.en: "Come home." A widow once lived with her small son in a bare attic, far from the homeland she had left, against her family's wishes, to marry a man who had since died and left them nothing. The happiest hours of the boy's life were when his mother gathered him up and told him of her father's house in the old country — the green lawns, the great trees, the wonderful meals. He had never seen it, yet it became the most beautiful place in the world to him, and he longed to go. Then one day a letter came. Inside was money for the journey and a slip of paper with two words in his grandfather's hand: "Come home." That is the heart of what Jesus says. He has gone ahead to the Father's house, and one day the word will come for us too.
blocks.es_reference: "Vuelve a casa." Una viuda vivía una vez con su pequeño hijo en un ático desnudo, lejos de la tierra natal que había dejado, contra los deseos de su familia, para casarse con un hombre que desde entonces había muerto y los había dejado sin nada. Las horas más felices del niño eran cuando su madre lo tomaba en brazos y le contaba de la casa de su abuelo en el viejo país — los prados verdes, los grandes árboles, las comidas maravillosas. Nunca la había visto, y sin embargo llegó a ser el lugar más hermoso del mundo para él, y anhelaba ir. Entonces un día llegó una carta. Dentro había dinero para el viaje y un papel con dos palabras de puño y letra del abuelo: "Vuelve a casa." Ese es el corazón de lo que dice Jesús. Ha ido delante a la casa del Padre, y un día la palabra vendrá también para nosotros.

blocks.en: II. "I Am the Way, the Truth, and the Life"
blocks.es_reference: II. "Yo soy el camino, y la verdad, y la vida"

blocks.en: Thomas, ever the honest doubter, broke in: "Lord, we do not know where You are going, and how can we know the way?" Jesus did not hand him a map or a set of directions. He gave him a Person: "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me" (John 14:6). Each word answers a need. He is the Way — and the opposite of the way is being lost. Not every road reaches the destination, however sincerely it is traveled; Jesus said there are finally only two roads, the broad way that many take and that ends in destruction, and the narrow way of humility and obedience that few find. And He says plainly that He Himself is the one Way to the Father; every other road that promises to reach God while going around Him falls short. He is the Truth — not merely a teacher of true things but the Truth in person, so that to know Him is to know what is real. He is the Life — and the person without Him is not merely uneducated or unlucky but spiritually dead, alive to the world yet dead to God. Only Christ can make such a one truly alive, giving both an abundant life now and eternal life forever.
blocks.es_reference: Tomás, siempre el dudador honesto, interrumpió: "Señor, no sabemos a dónde vas; ¿cómo, pues, podemos saber el camino?" Jesús no le entregó un mapa ni un juego de indicaciones. Le dio una Persona: ⚡ "Yo soy el camino, y la verdad, y la vida; nadie viene al Padre, sino por mí" (Juan 14:6). Cada palabra responde a una necesidad. Él es el Camino — y lo opuesto del camino es estar perdido. No todo camino llega al destino, por sincero que sea el que lo recorre; Jesús dijo que al fin hay solo dos caminos, el ancho que muchos toman y que termina en destrucción, y el angosto de humildad y obediencia que pocos hallan. Y dice llanamente que él mismo es el único Camino al Padre; todo otro camino que promete llegar a Dios rodeándole se queda corto. Él es la Verdad — no meramente un maestro de cosas verdaderas sino la Verdad en persona, de modo que conocerle a él es conocer lo que es real. Él es la Vida — y la persona sin él no es meramente ignorante ni desafortunada sino espiritualmente muerta, viva al mundo pero muerta a Dios. Solo Cristo puede hacer vivo de veras a tal persona, dando tanto una vida abundante ahora como vida eterna para siempre.

blocks.en: "I didn't say religion." As a restless young man, Josh McDowell tried church, prestige, and parties, and found his life empty — "a living hell," he said. Drawn in spite of himself to a group of Christians whose joy he could not explain, he leaned back in his chair and demanded, "Tell me — what changed your lives?" A young woman looked him straight in the eye and said two words: "Jesus Christ." He snapped back that he was fed up with religion. She answered, "Mister, I didn't say religion. I said Jesus Christ." That distinction undid him, and after long study of the evidence he came to confess that Jesus is exactly who He claimed to be — the only way to the Father.
blocks.es_reference: "No dije religión." De joven inquieto, Josh McDowell probó la iglesia, el prestigio y las fiestas, y halló su vida vacía — "un infierno en vida," dijo. Atraído a pesar de sí mismo por un grupo de cristianos cuyo gozo no podía explicar, se recostó en su silla y exigió: "Díganme — ¿qué cambió sus vidas?" Una joven lo miró directo a los ojos y dijo dos palabras: "Jesucristo." Él replicó que estaba harto de la religión. Ella respondió: "Señor, no dije religión. Dije Jesucristo." Esa distinción lo deshizo, y tras largo estudio de la evidencia llegó a confesar que Jesús es exactamente quien afirmó ser — el único camino al Padre.

blocks.en: III. "I Am the True Vine"
blocks.es_reference: III. "Yo soy la vid verdadera"

blocks.en: Still in that room, Jesus reached for a picture every one of them knew, and gave the last of the seven sayings: "I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser" (John 15:1). Near London there grows a grapevine called the Great Vine, planted over two hundred and fifty years ago, with a root two feet thick and branches stretching two hundred feet, still bearing hundreds of pounds of grapes each year. But Jesus is the true vine, the real source of life, and the Father is the gardener. A good vinedresser is far more than a farmer: he knows each vine intimately, how it fares from year to year, what it needs and when, even the exact place and angle to cut. And cut he does. "Every branch that bears fruit He prunes, that it may bear more fruit" (John 15:2). Pruning is not punishment; it is love with a knife. Sometimes the Father cuts away what is plainly dead, but often He cuts away even the good and the better, so that we may have the best. It hurts, but it helps. Paul begged three times for his thorn to be taken away, and instead was told, "My grace is sufficient for you"; the very thing he wanted removed was the Gardener's tool to make him more fruitful.
blocks.es_reference: Aún en aquel aposento, Jesús tomó una imagen que todos ellos conocían, y dio la última de las siete declaraciones: ⚡ "Yo soy la vid verdadera, y mi Padre es el labrador" (Juan 15:1). Cerca de Londres crece una vid llamada la Gran Vid, plantada hace más de doscientos cincuenta años, con una raíz de dos pies de grueso y ramas que se extienden doscientos pies, que aún da cientos de libras de uvas cada año. Pero Jesús es la vid verdadera, la fuente real de vida, y el Padre es el labrador. Un buen viñador es mucho más que un granjero: conoce cada vid íntimamente, cómo le va de año en año, qué necesita y cuándo, aun el lugar y el ángulo exactos donde cortar. Y corta. ⚡ "Todo aquel que lleva fruto, lo limpia, para que lleve más fruto" (Juan 15:2). La poda no es castigo; es amor con un cuchillo. A veces el Padre corta lo que está claramente muerto, pero a menudo corta aun lo bueno y lo mejor, para que tengamos lo mejor de todo. Duele, pero ayuda. Pablo rogó tres veces que le fuese quitado su aguijón, y en cambio se le dijo: "Bástate mi gracia"; lo mismo que quería quitar era la herramienta del Labrador para hacerlo más fructífero.

blocks.en: IV. "Abide in Me"
blocks.es_reference: IV. "Permaneced en mí"

blocks.en: At the center of the picture is one repeated command: "Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in Me" (John 15:4). The word "abide" is the verb behind the word "abode" — a dwelling place. To abide in Christ is not merely to know facts about Him, nor even only to pray, but to live with Him in a close, family relationship, aware of Him beside us every moment of every day. And mark this carefully: fruit is not automatic. Many imagine that a real Christian will simply produce fruit on his own; but Jesus says fruit comes only by abiding — and abiding is not automatic either, or He would not have had to command it. That very night every one of them would fail to abide, Peter most of all.
blocks.es_reference: En el centro de la imagen hay un mandato repetido: ⚡ "Permaneced en mí, y yo en vosotros. Como el pámpano no puede llevar fruto por sí mismo, si no permanece en la vid, así tampoco vosotros, si no permanéis en mí" (Juan 15:4). La palabra "permanecer" (morar) es el verbo detrás de la palabra "morada" — un lugar donde se habita. Permanecer en Cristo no es meramente saber datos acerca de él, ni siquiera solo orar, sino vivir con él en una relación estrecha, de familia, conscientes de él a nuestro lado cada momento de cada día. Y note esto con cuidado: el fruto no es automático. Muchos imaginan que un verdadero cristiano producirá fruto por sí solo; pero Jesús dice que el fruto viene solo por permanecer — y permanecer tampoco es automático, o no habría tenido que mandarlo. Esa misma noche cada uno de ellos fallaría en permanecer, Pedro más que todos.

blocks.en: Staying plugged in. It is like charging a phone. The battery runs low through the day, so we plug it into the power; but if we grow impatient and unplug it to use it before it has charged, it dies again. So with us: the life and power we need flow only while we stay connected to the Vine. Stuart Briscoe once preached on abiding in Christ to a hundred young believers crammed into a building in Cold-War Poland. Ten minutes in, the lights went out and the room went black, and he preached on in the dark. When the lights blinked back, he was startled to see every person on their knees — and they stayed on their knees long after he finished. "Your teaching was new to us," one told him. "We wanted to make sure we were abiding in Christ."
blocks.es_reference: Permanecer conectado. Es como cargar un teléfono. La batería se agota durante el día, así que lo conectamos a la corriente; pero si nos impacientamos y lo desconectamos para usarlo antes de que se cargue, se apaga otra vez. Así con nosotros: la vida y el poder que necesitamos fluyen solo mientras permanecemos conectados a la Vid. Stuart Briscoe predicó una vez sobre permanecer en Cristo a cien jóvenes creyentes apretujados en un edificio en la Polonia de la Guerra Fría. A los diez minutos las luces se apagaron y el cuarto quedó a oscuras, y él siguió predicando en la oscuridad. Cuando las luces volvieron, se sorprendió al ver a cada persona de rodillas — y siguieron de rodillas mucho después de que él terminó. "Su enseñanza era nueva para nosotros," le dijo uno. "Queríamos asegurarnos de estar permaneciendo en Cristo."

blocks.en: V. Bearing Much Fruit
blocks.es_reference: V. Llevar mucho fruto

blocks.en: "I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing" (John 15:5). Apart from Christ we can do exactly nothing of eternal worth, but abiding in Him the life flows and the fruit comes. And fruit is more than evangelism alone, though it surely includes the winning of souls. Every believer bears fruit by exercising the gifts God has given — teaching, hospitality, mercy, prayer — and above all the fruit of the Spirit: "love, joy, peace" and the rest (Galatians 5:22–23). When the watching world sees a people marked by that fruit, it sees something it cannot explain and cannot produce. And when there is no fruit, the trouble is an attachment problem — something blocking the flow of life from the Vine — and the cure is not to give up but to clear away the sin and abide afresh. All of this, Jesus says, is "to My Father's glory, that you bear much fruit." So the two sayings come together: the Way brings us home to the Father, and the Vine keeps us alive and fruitful all the way there. Have you come to the Father by the one Way? Then stay close to the Vine, and let His life bear its fruit through you.
blocks.es_reference: ⚡ "Yo soy la vid, vosotros los pámpanos; el que permanece en mí, y yo en él, éste lleva mucho fruto; porque sin mí nada podéis hacer" (Juan 15:5). Aparte de Cristo no podemos hacer nada de valor eterno, pero permaneciendo en él la vida fluye y el fruto viene. Y el fruto es más que la evangelización sola, aunque ciertamente la incluye. Todo creyente lleva fruto al ejercer los dones que Dios le ha dado — enseñar, hospedar, tener misericordia, orar — y sobre todo el fruto del Espíritu: "amor, gozo, paz" y lo demás (Gálatas 5:22–23). Cuando el mundo que observa ve a un pueblo marcado por ese fruto, ve algo que no puede explicar ni producir. Y cuando no hay fruto, el problema es de conexión — algo que bloquea el flujo de vida de la Vid — y el remedio no es rendirse sino quitar el pecado y permanecer de nuevo. Todo esto, dice Jesús, es "para la gloria de mi Padre, que llevéis mucho fruto." Así que las dos declaraciones se unen: el Camino nos lleva a casa, al Padre, y la Vid nos mantiene vivos y fructíferos todo el trayecto. ¿Ha venido usted al Padre por el único Camino? Entonces permanezca cerca de la Vid, y deje que su vida lleve su fruto a través de usted.

sa.prompt: Explain how Jesus comforts His troubled disciples with the promise of the Father's house (John 14:1-3).
sa.model: With their hearts breaking, Jesus said, Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in Me. In My Father's house are many mansions, and I go to prepare a place for you, and I will come again and receive you to Myself. He comforts them by promising that heaven is a real place, the Father's house, the believer's true home, not wishful thinking. The word for mansions means rooms or abiding places, prepared by Christ Himself, and one day He will return to bring His people there.

sa.prompt: Explain "I am the way" and why Jesus is the only way to the Father (John 14:6).
sa.model: When Thomas said they did not know the way, Jesus answered, I am the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me. He did not give a map but Himself, a Person. The opposite of the way is being lost, and not every road reaches God however sincerely it is traveled. Jesus said there are only two roads, the broad way to destruction and the narrow way few find. He is the only way to the Father; every other road that bypasses Him falls short, for no one comes to the Father except through Him.

sa.prompt: Explain "I am the truth" and "I am the life" (John 14:6).
sa.model: Jesus is the truth, not merely a teacher of true things but the Truth in person, so that to know Him is to know what is real. He is also the life. The person without Christ is spiritually dead, alive to the world but dead to God. Only Jesus can make such a one truly alive, giving both an abundant life now and eternal life forever. So the Way, the Truth, and the Life are not three separate gifts but the one Christ who brings us to the Father, shows us reality, and raises us from spiritual death.

sa.prompt: Explain "I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser" (John 15:1).
sa.model: Jesus said, I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser. He is the true vine, the real source of spiritual life and nourishment, just as branches draw everything they have from the vine. The Father is the gardener, the vinedresser, who is far more than a farmer: He knows each vine intimately, what it needs and when, and even the exact place to cut. So Jesus is the life and the Father lovingly tends His people, working to make each one more fruitful as a good vinedresser tends his vines.

sa.prompt: Explain how and why the Father prunes the branches (John 15:2).
sa.model: Jesus said that every branch that bears fruit the Father prunes, that it may bear more fruit. Pruning is not punishment but love with a knife. Sometimes the Father cuts away what is plainly dead, but often He cuts away even the good and the better so that we may have the best. It hurts, but it helps us grow. Paul begged three times for his thorn to be removed, and was told instead, My grace is sufficient for you; the very thing he wanted gone was the Gardener's tool to make him more fruitful.

sa.prompt: Explain what it means to "abide in Me" (John 15:4).
sa.model: Jesus said, Abide in Me, and I in you; the branch cannot bear fruit unless it abides in the vine. The word abide is the verb behind the word abode, a dwelling place. To abide in Christ is not merely to know facts about Him, nor even only to pray, but to remain connected to Him and live with Him in a close, family relationship, aware of Him beside us every day. As His word remains in us we stay joined to Him, and only by this daily abiding can the life of the vine flow into the branch.

sa.prompt: Explain "apart from Me you can do nothing" (John 15:5).
sa.model: Jesus said, I am the vine, you are the branches; he who abides in Me bears much fruit, for without Me you can do nothing. A branch cut off from the vine can produce nothing; so apart from Christ we can do nothing of eternal worth. We depend on Him entirely, as a branch depends on the vine for all its life and sap. It is like a phone that runs only while it stays connected to the power. As long as we remain connected to Christ, His life flows through us and the fruit comes; cut off from Him, we wither.

sa.prompt: Explain why bearing fruit is not automatic and how it comes (John 15:4-5).
sa.model: Many imagine that a real Christian will automatically produce fruit, but Cook insists this is not what Jesus says. Fruit comes only by abiding in Christ, and abiding is not automatic either, or Jesus would not have had to command it; that very night the disciples failed to abide, Peter most of all. The branch bears fruit only while it stays connected to the vine. So fruit comes not by trying harder on our own but by remaining joined to Christ, letting His life flow through us, the way a branch draws from the vine.

sa.prompt: Describe the kinds of fruit the abiding believer bears (John 15:5-8; Galatians 5).
sa.model: Cook teaches that fruit is more than evangelism alone, though it surely includes winning souls. Every believer bears fruit by exercising the gifts God has given, such as teaching, hospitality, mercy, and prayer, and above all the fruit of the Spirit named in Galatians 5: love, joy, peace, and the rest. Abiding in Christ also leads to persistent prayer and selfless service to others. When the watching world sees a people marked by such love and fruit, it sees something it cannot explain or produce on its own, and it is drawn to Christ.

sa.prompt: How do "the Way" and "the true Vine" fit together, and what do they call us to?
sa.model: The two sayings answer the two deepest questions of the soul. As the Way, Jesus brings us home to the Father, for no one comes to the Father except through Him. As the true Vine, He keeps us alive and fruitful all the way there, since apart from Him we can do nothing. So the Way gets us to the Father's house, and the Vine sustains us on the journey. Together they call us to come to the Father by the one Way, Christ, and then to abide close to the Vine so that His life bears much fruit through us.
